project.title: Managing usage-based billing for Microsoft 365 Copilot
project.audience: Microsoft 365 administrators; secondary Azure cost administrators

intent.customerProblem: Administrators need to understand how eligible Copilot usage is connected to Azure billing, governed, validated, and monitored.
intent.valueProposition: Usage-based billing can expand access to supported Copilot experiences while keeping policy scope, usage, and cost visible.
intent.viewerOutcome: The viewer can explain the connect-govern-observe model and identify required checks before enabling usage-based billing.
learningObjectives: Understand how a Microsoft 365 billing policy connects eligible usage to an Azure billing scope.
Identify how users, groups, and supported services are governed by the policy.
Validate a configuration without assuming that usage reports update instantly.
Distinguish budget alerts from controls that automatically stop consumption.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription and resource group in the same tenant
Appropriate Azure permissions on the billing scope
An eligible user and supported service for validation
licensing: Eligibility and Copilot Credit consumption depend on the supported experience, license, and action.
warnings: Not every Copilot interaction necessarily creates a usage charge.
Billing-policy budgets and standard Azure budget alerts do not automatically stop usage.
Usage and cost reporting can be delayed.
limitations: The product UI is simplified conceptual UI, not a pixel-exact tutorial.
No live Microsoft 365 tenant or Azure billing configuration was changed or tested.
Current navigation labels require product review before publication.

scenes.voiceover: Usage-based billing lets your organization pay for supported Copilot services and AI experiences as they're used.
scenes.visualGuidance: Activate dormant service tiles only when a request reaches them, then emit a measured credit token into a cost counter.

screenCapture.reason: Conceptual animation communicates eligible usage more clearly.

scenes.voiceover: In Microsoft 365, create a billing policy, then connect an Azure subscription and resource group.
scenes.visualGuidance: Populate Subscription and Resource group in simplified Microsoft 365 admin chrome, then lock the policy to an Azure billing-scope tile.

screenCapture.reason: The evolving UI is better represented by durable conceptual labels.

reviewFlags: Confirm current navigation labels before publication.

scenes.purpose: Explain governance and the budget limitation.
scenes.voiceover: Scope the policy to eligible users or groups, and connect a supported service. A budget can send alerts, but it doesn't automatically stop usage.
scenes.visualGuidance: Add a fictional group and service, then show usage crossing a budget threshold and continuing after an alert appears.

screenCapture.reason: Synthetic UI makes the alert-versus-enforcement distinction explicit.

reviewFlags: Do not imply that a budget enforces a hard stop.

scenes.voiceover: Validate the setup with an eligible user and supported experience. Features and actions can consume different amounts of Copilot Credits.
scenes.visualGuidance: Send one test request through the policy, then resolve it into differently sized credit markers without exact quantities.

screenCapture.reason: No live tenant is available; show the documented loop conceptually.

reviewFlags: Do not claim a live tenant test or exact credit quantities.

scenes.purpose: Show monitoring across Microsoft 365 and Azure.
scenes.voiceover: Microsoft 365 reports show usage. Azure Cost Management adds cost analysis, forecasts, and alerts. Allow time for charges and reports to appear.
scenes.visualGuidance: Reveal policy and agent rows in a Credits report, then grow Actual cost and Forecast signals in Azure Cost analysis with a clock badge between them.

screenCapture.surface: Microsoft 365 reports and Azure Cost Management
screenCapture.reason: Simplified surfaces keep the relationship legible.

scenes.purpose: Close with prerequisites and the operating model.
scenes.voiceover: Before you begin, confirm the required Microsoft 365 and Azure permissions. With billing connected, scoped, and monitored, you can expand access while keeping costs visible.
scenes.visualGuidance: Verify Microsoft 365 and Azure role badges, then align the connected billing scope, governed policy, and observable cost signal.

screenCapture.reason: A hand-stitched summary is clearer than another product surface.

reviewFlags: Confirm role wording in final product review.

review.confidenceRationale: The operating model and caveats are grounded in current Microsoft Learn sources; navigation labels remain subject to product change.
sourceGaps: The Microsoft 365 Cost management experience may change after the research date.
A live customer tenant was not available for UI verification.

localizationNotes: Do not rely on color alone for state.
